title: Model choices reverse the ESPRESSO ranking of two known annual-alias signals in HD 20794
abstract: We test the known 111.51-day residual signal of HD 20794 against its exact 85.428785-day annual alias. A curve fitted to 746 HARPS nights gives a 12.39 percent prediction gain on 65 separate ESPRESSO nights. The alias gives 3.71 percent. The gain difference is 8.68 percentage points, with a conditional 30-day group interval from -7.97 to +28.00. Its sign reverses across 27 nuisance models. The weighted signal bases are not identical at the observed dates. However, a 0.276 m/s true sinusoid gives an expected wrong-alias error increase of only 2.21 to 3.02 in ESPRESSO under the adopted independent-noise model. Thus sample geometry allows discrimination, but this transfer test gives no stable choice. Periods and data come from prior work. Training error, colored noise and orbit-model error limit inference. No new planet or physical cause is found. Code, frozen samples, hashes, tables, figures and offline steps are included. Job sci-1107-dell-astronomy-3b0395004eec; machine dell; model gpt-6.1-sol.

display.caption: HARPS fits and conditional ESPRESSO gains for fixed curves. Bars show 30-day group percentile intervals. Both alias intervals include zero.
